items.headline: Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei calls for an industry-wide AI slowdown
items.summary: In an essay titled "We Must Pace the Frontier," Amodei warned that increasingly capable AI agents could act against human goals and potentially "take over the internet" within six to twelve months, urging common safety standards across frontier labs. OpenAI's Sam Altman and Tesla's Elon Musk both publicly endorsed the call within days.

items.headline: Chinese state media dismisses Amodei's AI slowdown call as 'self-serving'
items.summary: State-affiliated Chinese outlets pushed back on Dario Amodei's call for a global pacing of frontier AI development, framing it as an attempt by U.S. labs to lock in their lead, underscoring the geopolitical divide over AI safety coordination.

items.headline: Microsoft publishes draft 'Humanist AI' code of conduct
items.summary: Microsoft AI, led by Mustafa Suleyman, released a code of conduct requiring its first-party MAI models to remain under meaningful human control, with absolute bans on cyberattacks, nuclear weapons development and deepfake production; the draft is open for six weeks of public comment before guiding model development in 2027.

items.headline: Bernie Sanders and Steve Bannon join AI skeptics at Washington 'Pro-Human' conference
items.summary: An unusual left-right coalition gathered in Washington to press Congress for new curbs on rapidly accelerating AI development, reflecting growing bipartisan unease about the technology's pace even as lawmakers remain divided on how to regulate it.

items.headline: Agility Robotics unveils Digit 5, its first humanoid built to work beside people without safety cages
items.summary: The new-generation robot uses AI-driven collision-avoidance software and additional sensors to detect nearby workers and respond by stopping, repositioning, or sitting down; upgraded leg actuators let it repeatedly lift up to 50 pounds. Agility says early customer access begins in 2027.

items.headline: Apple opens its Gemini-powered Siri AI to the public in English
items.summary: Apple's rebuilt Siri, running on custom models distilled from Google's Gemini under a reported deal, is now broadly available in English and can act on on-screen content, emails, messages and photos; rollout to the EU and China is delayed for regulatory reasons.

items.headline: Anthropic launches Claude for Financial Advisors
items.summary: Unveiled at the Future Proof Festival, the new suite connects Claude to custodians and platforms including BlackRock, Schwab and Vanguard, aiming to streamline advisor workflows such as portfolio research, CRM updates and client communication.

items.headline: Cloudflare begins blocking 'mixed-use' AI crawlers by default
items.summary: New Cloudflare defaults taking effect this week block crawlers that blend search indexing, real-time AI-agent browsing and model training into one user agent from any ad-supported page, pressuring AI companies to separate those functions or pay publishers for training access.

items.headline: Google DeepMind releases AlphaGenome Atlas, mapping 9 billion possible human DNA mutations
items.summary: The free public database predicts the molecular effects of every possible single-letter DNA change in the human genome, condensed via a new AlphaGenome Variant Impact score; researchers at the Broad Institute have already used it to identify a rare disease-linked variant.

items.headline: DeepSeek releases V4.1-Flash, an open-weight multimodal model beating rivals on benchmarks
items.summary: The Chinese lab's new Mixture-of-Experts model supports million-token context and native multimodal input, with benchmark results said to exceed OpenAI's GPT-5.6 Sol and Anthropic's Claude Opus 5 while remaining open-source under an MIT license.

items.headline: OpenAI launches GPT-6 Astra, its first model to cross a 'Critical' cybersecurity risk threshold
items.summary: OpenAI's new flagship model tops benchmarks in computer use, coding and science, but during safety testing it independently discovered and chained two zero-day vulnerabilities, prompting OpenAI to disclose them to maintainers and train the public model to refuse advanced cyber tasks.
